FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Do not hang items from the mirror or cover the windshield with decals that may obstruct the view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Keep headlamps, backup lights, brake lights and taillights clean because dirty lenses can cut their effectiveness by 50 percent. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Check the seat and mirror settings before starting to drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Set the seat high enough to see the road clearly, using a cushion if needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
Do not place the seat so far forward that steering becomes difficult. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Set the interior rearview mirror to show the view through the back window. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
Adjust side mirrors to show the sides, with the vehicle side visible when leaning slightly forward. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Set a day-and-night mirror for the lighting conditions in which you will drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
A head restraint is intended to reduce whiplash in a rear impact. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
Adjust the head restraint so that it contacts the back of the head. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: FXP0030
Montana makes the driver responsible for ensuring occupants are properly belted or secured in child safety seats, subject to the listed legal exceptions [FXP0030] [A01].
Source: [FXP0030 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A01
Use the safety belt on every trip, including short trips at low speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A01
Before leaving, fasten your belt and check that passengers are using belts or child restraints. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A01
Lock the vehicle doors before driving away. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A01
A two-part belt system requires both the lap portion and the shoulder portion for its intended protection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A01
With an automatic shoulder belt, buckle the lap belt too. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A01
Using only one portion of a lap-and-shoulder system substantially reduces protection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A01
An unrestrained occupant can strike and seriously injure other people in the vehicle during a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

Misconceptions: A shoulder belt alone does not replace a lap belt, and an airbag does not replace the restraint system.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: adjust, buckle, check; keep the restraint matched to the rider and seat position.
Glossary: Head restraint; rearview mirror; lap belt; shoulder belt; booster seat; rear-facing child seat; special mobile equipment.
Dynamic facts: The child-restraint age-and-weight threshold is withheld because the page uses conflicting formulations; current monetary penalties and quantitative crash analogies also remain debt.
